label: es-e1a
change: NTSD 2.4's seven content packages move from NTSDCore to the game-side target NTSDContent (1,519 pure renames, .gitattributes following). Core gains OriginalContentLocation (the app bundle's folders, else a lazily looked-up fallback bundle: the old two-level rule) and no longer uses Bundle.module; the six loaders, OriginalRuntimeLoadingPackages and OriginalMacRuntimeLoading take it; the session builds it from --resources or the main bundle plus the host's new contentFallback; the six hosts give NTSDContent.fallback. Tests keep every call site through Bundle overloads in NTSDContentLocations.swift; two #filePath hash tests follow the path. The built bundle is NTSDNative_NTSDContent.bundle (.resources on Windows); 17 active tools follow, frozen producers and references unchanged (tools/finalize_application_*, verify_application_*, oracle_replay_*.py, prepare_application_catalog_package_validation.py, app_e2e_*reference.json). Harness: mlgate.sh's tested-tree step now stages with git add -A in a copy of the index; matrix.py and ios_app.py take NTSD_XPLAT_OUT for their build and run folders.

review.by: a separate read-only agent, 2026-10-18, on the staged index before the gates
review.verdict: behaviour-neutral; no required code fix. Loader lookups and errors identical to HEAD's; the fallback is evaluated only where Bundle.module was; @Sendable fallback not MainActor-isolated, no traps in Swift 5 mode; every test call resolves to exactly one overload, fake-.app tests still never fall back; .gitattributes yields byte-identical attributes at the new paths (5,763 lines); Core does not depend on NTSDContent; app_e2e.compare ignores the printed resources path; read-order.json is a pure prefix rename.
review.requiredFix: mlgate.sh's tested-tree step (read-tree HEAD plus `git diff --name-only` paths) drops deletions under rename detection: E1a's recorded native tree would have held the resources twice. Fixed (git add -A in a copy of the index) before the gate; the step's tree was checked equal to the staged index.
